findings.title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The totpStep1 value in the Lithuanian account bundle is now the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions for OTP setup. The edit was meant to remove HTML links but copied the wrong language.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The loginTotpStep1 value in the Lithuanian login bundle is now the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian instructions. The change was meant to strip anchor tags but inserted the wrong language.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file uses Traditional characters
findings.body: The new totpStep1 value in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle uses Traditional characters such as mobile-phone and application words written in Traditional form. Users with Simplified Chinese locale will see Traditional text. The file should use Simplified characters like the surrounding entries.

findings.title: Missing anchors in translation are never detected
findings.body: santizeAnchors only loops over anchor tags found in the translated value and checks each against English. It never checks that every anchor from the English source was consumed. A translation that deletes a required link entirely will therefore pass with no error, resulting in broken UI where the link is silently missing but the build stays green.

findings.title: Anchor mismatch error lacks key and file
findings.body: The message added for a changed anchor contains only the tag text and the words in original string, without the message key or file name. The Illegal HTML message in the same file includes both key and file. When verification fails on a large bundle the maintainer cannot locate the offending key without reproducing locally.

findings.title: Verbatim compare causes false positive on br tag formatting
findings.body: The verifier compares OWASP sanitizer output verbatim to the input. The sanitizer normalizes a self-closing break from br-slash form to br-space-slash form. A safe translation using the first form is therefore reported as Illegal HTML even though it is semantically identical. The PR had to rewrite more than twenty existing translations only to add that space, proving future contributions will be falsely rejected.

findings.title: Missing English file crashes verifier with RuntimeException
findings.body: If the English counterpart file cannot be opened, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException. The public verify method is declared to throw MojoExecutionException for IO problems. A single missing English file will therefore crash the theme-verifier plugin with a stack trace instead of producing a readable verification failure.

findings.title: HTML detection is case-sensitive
findings.body: The patterns for detecting HTML and anchor tags only match lowercase tag names. HTML tag names are case-insensitive, so an English source containing uppercase tags like B or A would be classified as containing no HTML and select the wrong sanitizer policy, mishandling a matching translation.

findings.title: Illegal HTML fixture is truncated
findings.body: The fixture value ends with open-div without the final closing bracket. The test therefore exercises a truncated tag rather than a proper disallowed element. It can pass for the wrong reason and does not document the intended illegal-tag case.

findings.title: No positive test for valid translations
findings.body: All tests assert that bad fixtures produce an error, but none asserts that good fixtures produce zero errors. For example there is no check that the valid English file or a translation with allowed formatting passes cleanly. A verifier that false-positives on every legitimate message would still pass the suite.
